estimateBasis: Focused engineering hours for one experienced TypeScript developer, including automated tests and a short evidence note. Product studies, review latency, and unknown provider defects are excluded.

milestones.title: Honest control loop
milestones.exit: A typed command can propose, approve, run, verify, review, and recover one bounded task.

milestones.title: Voice control
milestones.exit: Voice reaches the same command boundary with explicit capture and correct interruption semantics.

milestones.title: Trustworthy supervision
milestones.exit: Requirements, conflicts, approvals, budgets, privacy, and failure recovery behave correctly.

milestones.title: Supervised writer release
milestones.exit: The website workflow and regression suite prove the P0 claim.

milestones.title: Supervised team
milestones.exit: Read-only work, isolated writers, scheduling, integration, and local interpretation pass the P1 gate.

stories.title: Bootstrap a repeatable extension
stories.claim: A contributor can install, lint, test, package, and launch the VS Code extension from documented commands.
acceptance: CI runs the same lint, test, and package commands as local development.
A fresh checkout launches the extension development host.
No A00 workflow or spike source is part of the product branch.

stories.title: Open a durable Piarre project
stories.claim: Opening a trusted repository creates or replays a durable Piarre project and shows its Work view.
acceptance: The event log is authoritative and the project snapshot is a projection.
Duplicate command IDs do not duplicate effects.
Every state-changing command rejects a stale project revision.
Restart reproduces the same observable project state.

stories.title: Turn text into a reviewable task
stories.claim: A typed goal creates a proposal that a developer can inspect before any workspace write.
acceptance: The proposal names requirements, scope, dependencies, checks, budget, and plan version.
Invalid interpreter output is rejected at the boundary.
No workspace write occurs before visual approval.

stories.title: Run one bounded coding task
stories.claim: An approved task runs through one capability-driven worker contract while a second writer remains blocked.
acceptance: The adapter reports observed capabilities instead of relying on provider names.
Start, observe, steer when supported, interrupt, and inspect share one behavior contract.
Workspace and approved-command scopes are enforced.
A deterministic mock worker and the first real adapter pass the same contract.

stories.title: Verify before review
stories.claim: A finished run advances only through revision-bound verification evidence.
acceptance: A finished run enters Needs verification.
Evidence records plan version, workspace revision, and an outcome of passed, failed, or observed.
Required current checks are necessary for Needs review.
Worker completion text cannot accept a task.

stories.title: Review and accept current evidence
stories.claim: The developer reviews the exact diff and evidence before accepting the current revision.
acceptance: The Review view distinguishes passed checks, failed checks, observations, and worker claims.
Acceptance binds the project revision, plan version, and workspace revision.
A later relevant edit marks prior evidence stale.

stories.title: Stop without pretending to roll back
stories.claim: Stopping work preserves partial changes and reports uncertainty until the worker and disk are reconciled.
acceptance: Stop task requests interruption and inspects actual worker and workspace state.
Owned processes are reconciled.
Repeated stop requests converge on one result.
The UI never labels an unobserved run as stopped.

stories.title: Recover after restart
stories.claim: Restart restores durable work without repeating external actions or inventing a final run state.
acceptance: Running, interrupted, and Needs review states replay correctly.
Active external runs become unknown until inspected.
Workspace and worker observations are appended before scheduling resumes.
A lost acknowledgement does not repeat an external action.

stories.title: Speak and type through one command boundary
stories.claim: Explicit voice controls feed final transcripts into the same proposal path as typed commands.
acceptance: Start, mute, push-to-talk, and End have visible microphone state.
A mock voice adapter tests lifecycle and command routing without a key.
Mock voice makes no claim about recognition quality or provider behavior.
Credentials stay outside the Webview.

stories.title: Separate speech interruption from work interruption
stories.claim: Barge-in can silence speech without silently stopping coding.
acceptance: Stop speaking, Stop task, and Stop all dispatch separate domain actions.
Barge-in silences output while active coding continues.
Stop actions require resolved targets.
Ambiguous references request clarification and destructive actions require visual confirmation.

stories.title: Change a requirement during work
stories.claim: A spoken or typed correction updates affected work without invalidating unrelated progress.
acceptance: The correction creates a new requirement and plan version.
Only affected tasks are steered or replanned after policy validation.
Additional scope returns to review.
A stale run cannot satisfy the current task.

stories.title: Protect manual edits
stories.claim: Piarre detects concurrent manual changes and never silently overwrites them.
acceptance: The approved base revision is compared with current files before apply or acceptance.
Conflicts are visible and block acceptance.
Unrelated manual edits remain intact.

stories.title: Make authority and cost visible
stories.claim: Every consequential action shows its authority, scope, and enforceable budget before execution.
acceptance: Approval binds action, scope, plan version, base revision, duration, and project revision.
Network, install, secret, and destructive operations use distinct policy decisions.
Measured usage and estimates use separate labels.
Scheduling stops at enforceable limits.

stories.title: Control local data
stories.claim: The user can see, export, retain, and delete Piarre's local data without hidden recording.
acceptance: Settings disclose which provider receives audio, transcript, code, and output.
Raw audio is opt-in and stored outside the repository.
Exports omit secrets.
Local deletion is read back and verified without claiming provider-side deletion.

stories.title: Build and verify a local website
stories.claim: The built-in website workflow completes the product's supervised-writer golden path.
acceptance: The journey covers discovery, plan approval, one-worker implementation, mid-run correction, build verification, preview review, acceptance, restart recovery, and evidence-backed export.
Preview processes have explicit ownership and cleanup.
The UI distinguishes command success from unperformed visual review.

stories.title: Pass the supervised-writer release gate
stories.claim: Piarre earns its supervised-writer claim through repeatable fixture and live-adapter evidence.
acceptance: The golden path and twelve named regression scenarios run against deterministic fixtures.
Supported live adapters record current evidence.
The report distinguishes passed, failed, blocked, unsupported, and not tested.
No release claim relies on the retired A00 spike.

stories.title: Assign parallel read-only research
stories.claim: A read-only worker can gather bounded evidence while the supervised writer runs.
acceptance: Write-capable tools fail at the adapter boundary.
Research output attaches as evidence or a proposal.
Research cannot change policy, approval, or task state.

stories.title: Isolate every coding worker
stories.claim: Each coding run owns an isolated worktree and cannot share a write root.
acceptance: Every run records base revision, path, and ownership.
Two writers cannot receive the same working tree.
Cleanup is idempotent after review or cancellation.
Restart can recover active leases.

stories.title: Schedule by dependency and capability
stories.claim: The scheduler assigns only ready work and explains every blocked assignment.
acceptance: Dependencies, capabilities, approvals, budgets, and isolation constrain assignment.
Replayed scheduling does not create duplicate runs.
Concurrency limits are enforced deterministically.

stories.title: Integrate through review
stories.claim: Isolated worker output reaches the primary workspace only through an explicit integration review.
acceptance: Completion creates an integration-review task.
Overlapping files and conflicts are surfaced.
One approved change is imported at a time.
Integration invalidates affected evidence and requires verification of the new revision.

stories.title: Route commands through an optional local interpreter
stories.claim: A hosted OpenAI-compatible adapter and a small local adapter can emit the same untrusted proposal schema.
acceptance: Core policy never branches on provider name.
Invalid proposals are rejected at the boundary.
Capability, target, approval, and budget checks remain deterministic.
Invalid-action rate, ambiguity handling, latency, and memory are measured before support is advertised.

stories.title: Verify with a different worker
stories.claim: A worker that did not author a change can run bounded checks without accepting its own evidence.
acceptance: Author and verifier identities remain visible.
Verifier capabilities are enforced.
Verification attaches evidence but acceptance remains a user action.

stories.title: Pass the supervised-team release gate
stories.claim: One read-only worker and two isolated coding workers pass the supervised-team safety suite.
acceptance: Dependency, conflict, integration, cancellation, budget, stale-evidence, and recovery scenarios pass.
No coding workers share a write root.
The release report records supported and unsupported providers and hardware.
